chunks: He said: Al-Mudhaffar ibn Muhammad al-Warraq reported to me from Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam, who reported from Abu Saeed al-Hasan ibn Zakariyya al-Basri, who reported from Umar ibn al-Mukhtar, who reported from Abu Muhammad al-Barsi, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwaid, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad al-Baqir, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:

"How will it be for you, O Ali, when you stand at the brim of hellfire, and the Sirat has been stretched, and the people are told: 'Cross!' and you say to hellfire: 'This one is for me, and this one is for you'?"
Ali, peace be upon him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, who will be those [with me]?" He said: "Those are your Shi'ah, with you wherever you are."

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: Al-Sirat - The Bridge: the bridge stretched over hellfire that all must cross on Judgment Day
key_terms.جَهَنَّم: Jahannam - Hellfire: the abode of punishment in Islamic eschatology
key_terms.جُوزُوا: Juzu - Cross!: imperative to cross the Sirat bridge
key_terms.شَفِير: Shafir - Brim/edge: the precipice of hellfire where Ali will stand on Judgment Day
key_terms.شِيعَتُكَ: Shi'atuka - Your Shi'ah/followers: those loyal to Ali who will be with him

ai.seo_question: What role does Imam Ali play on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) addresses Imam Ali (AS), describing a scene on the Day of Judgment where Ali will stand at the brim of hellfire beside the Sirat bridge, directing people—some to salvation and some to punishment. When Ali asks who will be with him, the Prophet replies that his Shi‘ah (followers) will be with him wherever he goes. This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Baqir (AS) from his forefathers, reflects the early Muslim community’s understanding of loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt as the criterion for salvation, and was likely shared to reassure the faithful during times of persecution.
